result.evidence:
Audit: about 112 words, which is within range. There is no repetition of the excerpt and no fabricated stats or anecdotes.

c1: Grammatically, "back to wherever you happen to live" does complete the cut point. Logically it is muddled. The point should be that money leaves the US, but "wherever you happen to live" is vague. The next sentence then calls the remote person "a local worker who has no stake in the community", which confuses remote and local. The capital-export mechanism is never stated clearly.

c2: The reasoning shifts to local consumer spending ("rent and food", "local schools", "real town"). This is not why in-person presence matters for value creation, such as company-building or collaboration. The ending is abstract filler: "aren't even in the same league" and "get one set of results from the other".

c3: Length is fine and there are no fabrications. The voice is mostly direct, but it slips into vague hedging and loose phrasing ("absolutely none of it", "a bit more like a real town"). The confused referents weaken the economy of the prose.
